craft_playbook: Deliver the hook inside 2.5 seconds; viewers decide in under 2 on mobile.
Open with a pattern interrupt or curiosity gap; NEVER context/build-up or greetings.
Reverse structure: lead with the payoff (news, boldest number, verdict tease), explain after.
Include a concrete number in the hook when possible (price, 0-100, sales figure).
No dead air: trim silences; keep delivery slightly faster than conversational.
Bury nothing: the best moment goes first, not 15 seconds in.
One idea per beat; cut visuals every 2-3 seconds; open on motion or high-contrast frame.
End with a question that begs a comment + a loop-friendly closer (last line can feed the first).
Hook and content must match; clickbait mismatch kills retention and trust.
Front-load value beats: price/verdict by the midpoint, never last.

NEVER recycle a joke or catchphrase across videos — banned as overused: 'how is this even legal', '<rival> owners are sweating', 'means business', 'game-changer'. Each video needs its OWN fresh, specific, Indian-relatable humor (potholes, speed breakers, family weddings, the neighbour, EMIs).

Write for the SPOKEN voiceover: say 'driver-assist' not ADAS, 'four-wheel-drive' not 4XPLOR, 'low-range' not 4-Low, 'Newton-metres' not Nm. Short, easy-to-pronounce, easy-to-understand lines — no dense technical strings. Acronyms/short forms belong ONLY in on-screen pops (read, not spoken).
data_learnings: [high][process][no-wikipedia-2026-08] Wikipedia is REMOVED as a fact/spec source (specsource WikipediaSpecSource deleted; webresearch blocks wikipedia.org/wikiwand/dbpedia at tier 9; grounding uses tier-1 only; crawl now aliases research). It repeatedly shipped wrong India-market specs presented as verified fact (1.5L Fronx, wrong-Brezza turbo). Facts come ONLY from tier-1 authorities (CarDekho/CarWale/Autocar/ZigWheels) + official maker sites (Nexa). If none reachable, sheet is thin/empty on purpose — owner fills from the official site by hand; never inject an unsourced number. NOTE: Wikimedia Commons IMAGES (adapters/footage.py) are a SEPARATE licensed image source, still in use.

[high][mechanic][vision-fp-2026-08] Vision blocking is TIERED to cut false positives without weakening safety: readable_plate + watermark_or_logo_overlay HARD-block on a single frame (owner rule — plates blurred/excluded, never ripped/watermarked), but wrong_vehicle_type needs corroboration (>=2 frames of the SAME clip) before it quarantines — a car/aircraft glimpsed in ONE sampled frame (e.g. a helicopter through the Sierra's sunroof, a passing car, a reflection) is advisory, not a block. Implemented in quality/vqa.py blocking_fails(); autoloop + qa consume the corrected blocking_detail unchanged.

[high][process][step5-2026-08] Workflows are codified as SKILLS (charters/skills/*.md) — a charter says WHO an agent is, a skill says HOW to run one workflow (exact `carshorts ...` commands + gates). `carshorts skills` lists them; the headless agent auto-routes a task to the matching skill by trigger keywords and follows its steps verbatim (agents/skills.py route+compose_prompt), so it stops re-deriving (and drifting) the procedure each run. Add a new workflow as a skill, not as tribal knowledge. Seed set: source-footage, produce-video, ground-facts, publish-video, close-the-loop.

[high][process][step4-2026-08] Before rendering a car, run `carshorts footage <slug>` (footageplan): it reports clean distinct clips vs cuts (one clip per cut — the no-repeat rule), a per-angle histogram, missing essential angles (front/side/rear/interior/action), and any clip with NO cleared source in footage_sources.json/attributions.json. A footage-blocked render must surface this shopping list — not a vague 'needs footage'. The Tata Sierra proved it: after the vision gate pulled 4 plated/watermarked ad clips, only 4 clean clips remained (missing side+rear), all with unverified provenance.

[high][process][step4-2026-08] Provenance is a hard licensing gate, not paperwork: never let clips with unknown source sit in a car's own/ pool. `ingest` records source+licence to footage_sources.json; ripped/watermarked ad footage (readable plates, burned-in 'creative representation only' disclaimers — e.g. the Tata Sierra promo) is refused. Two free, no-attribution stock-video APIs (Pexels + Pixabay) via build_video_source() give resilience without paid spend.

[high][process][mg-hawk-2026-08] LEAD with real/press footage; concept stock (especially of OTHER cars) must NEVER lead a video — a stock "highway" clip put plated Mercedes G-Wagons in an MG hook. Vet fetched stock at FULL-RES for readable PLATES and RIVAL BADGES (a small thumbnail grid hid both). For an unreleased car with no real footage, pin the owner clips to hook/spec/value via a shot plan and let concept b-roll fill only peak/cta.

[high][mechanic][overlays-2026-08-03] Overlays went PREMIUM: retired the heavy Montserrat-Black + tech-cyan + thick meme-stroke look. Two selectable themes, auto-alternated per render for an A/B test (produce --overlay-theme luxe|frost|auto; recorded in manifest render.overlay_theme). A 'luxe' = thin/light weight, wide letter-spacing, boxless, champagne accent (owner's pick). B 'frost' = semibold in a smoked-glass panel, champagne rule. Both: generous TRACKING (the amateur->pro tell), ONE metallic accent (champagne #DEC58C, never cyan/yellow), no heavy stroke. When comparing performance, read overlay_theme from each video's manifest and attribute retention to the look.

[high][mechanic][overlays-2026-08-03] Count-up card bugfix: a unit label ('₹11.49L · EX-SHOWROOM') must NEVER share the giant number line — it clips off both frame edges. The card now splits on '·' into a small tracked kicker + the big value, and hard-clamps the value width to the safe box. Keep card 'show' text as VALUE · LABEL and the engine handles the split.

[high] Avoid looping footage: When a clip is shorter than the beat duration, it loops, which is a QA failure. Renderer should either trim the beat to the clip length or select a longer clip. For example, 'sierra_hero.mp4' is 5.2s but used for 6.2s.

[medium] Keep using question-based hooks that tease a surprising spec or value proposition (e.g., 'Kia crammed a 120 PS turbo...' or 'MG claims a thousand kilometres...') — these drove the highest engagement (Kia Sonet: 1557 views, MG Hector: 321 views with 8 likes). Avoid pure news/price-hike hooks (Hyundai Creta: 244 views, Mahindra Thar: 118-151 views) which underperformed. Script writer should lead with a provocative question or surprising fact in the first 5 seconds.

[medium] Shorten scripts to 70-90 words and 5 sections. The best performers (Kia Sonet: 71 words/5 sections, MG Hector: 81 words/5 sections, Tata Sierra: 72 words/5 sections) had higher retention (36-49%) than longer ones (Brezza: 139 words/6 sections at 34%, Nexon: 165 words/7 sections at 47% but only 27 views). Trim spec dumps and keep the script tight, especially the spec beat which is the worst drop-off point in multiple videos.

[high] Fix visual quality issues flagged in QA: avoid dark/blurry clips, watermarks, readable license plates, and repeated footage. The Tata Sierra draft had 3 repeated clips and multiple frames with readable plates/watermarks, violating the owner's #1 rule. Renderer should pre-screen assets for these issues and ensure each clip is used only once, possibly by expanding the stock pool.

[medium] For the spec beat, keep it concise and visual. Multiple videos (Creta, Scorpio-N, Thar) showed the biggest drop at the spec section (drop_by_beat: 0.65, 0.54, 0.81). Script writer should condense specs to 1-2 key numbers and pair them with strong visuals (e.g., action shots, not static stills) to maintain interest. Renderer should use dynamic footage during spec narration.

[low] Use the 'chatterbox' voice engine and 'Balearic Slide' music for better performance. The Kia Sonet (chatterbox) achieved 1557 views, while the Creta (edge) got only 244. The Thar with elevenlabs had low views (118-151). Stick with chatterbox for a consistent, engaging tone. Also, consider adding captions — none of the videos had them, and captions could improve retention.

[low] For comparison videos (like Sierra vs Creta), focus on a clear value proposition. The Sierra vs Creta draft had a great hook ('58k more, 45 more horses') but only 109 views, likely due to low sample size. However, the Tata Sierra standalone video (76 views) had a strong hook retention (drop_by_beat hook: 0.445) but suffered from visual issues. Ensure comparison videos have distinct, high-quality visuals for each car to avoid confusion.

[medium] Keep using question-based hooks: the Kia Sonet video with a question hook got 1557 views, while the Creta news hook got only 244. Also, the Swift deadpan question hook had 478 views with high retention (130% avg_view_pct), suggesting questions engage viewers.

[medium] Shorten the spec section: multiple videos (Sonet, Scorpio-N, Thar, Punch) show the worst retention drop at the 'spec' beat. For example, Sonet dropped 64.9% at spec, Scorpio-N dropped 54.1%. Trim spec details or present them more visually to maintain interest.

[medium] Avoid using overly dark or blurry stock footage: QA failures on Tata Sierra and Brezza show too_dark_or_blurry issues. For renderer: filter out low-quality clips before final render. For script writer: avoid phrases that might mismatch with available clips.

[high] Ensure no clip reuse: Tata Sierra failed QA due to repeated clips (sierra_sunroof, sierra_dash). For renderer: implement a check to prevent reuse of the same clip across cuts, or expand the stock footage pool.

[low] The Brezza video with only 40 views shows weak signal, but its retention curve dropped sharply after the first 20%, possibly due to the hype persona. For script writer: consider testing more deadpan or default personas for consistency, as the Sonet deadpan with question hook performed better.
